findings.passage: Trump tried to disqualify eligible voters and throw out lawfully cast ballots. Andrea fought back, co-leading a lawsuit with 24 states to block his unconstitutional voting order and winning in court when Trump’s Justice Department demanded Massachusetts voter data. When Trump directed the Post Office to take control of mail-in voting, requiring states to overhaul their entire election systems in a matter of weeks, Andrea co-led a coalition of 25 states to sue to stop it, and won a preliminary injunction blocking the rule from taking effect before November.
findings.note: Campaign site text (page last modified 2026-09-17) describing her lawsuits as Attorney General against a federal voting order, a federal demand for state voter data, and a federal rule on mail-in voting. It does not mention photo ID or documentary proof of citizenship by name. Date is the page's last-modified date, not the date of the lawsuits.

findings.passage: “Elections should be free, fair and accessible,” Campbell said in the statement. “The Trump Administration’s attempt to disqualify eligible voters and throw out lawfully cast ballots is plainly unconstitutional. We will not stand by while the President tries to impose unlawful barriers to the ballot box.”
findings.note: Boston Globe quotes Campbell's statement on joining a 19-state suit against the March 2025 executive order that called for proof of citizenship to register and for limits on counting mail and absentee ballots.

findings.passage: Imposing “extraordinarily burdensome proof of citizenship requirements for voter registration” would “disenfranchise countless eligible Massachusetts voters,” according to Campbell’s statement.
findings.note: Globe sentence quoting fragments of Campbell's own statement about documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration. Only the quoted fragments are her words.

findings.motion: Joined multistate federal suit in Boston against the March 2025 executive order on proof of citizenship for voter registration and mail-ballot counting
findings.note: Campbell signed on as one of 19 attorneys general plaintiffs. The suit asks a court to declare the order's provisions unconstitutional and void.

findings.passage: “Though the President may wish he had unlimited power to restrict voting rights, the Constitution gives states – not the White House – the authority to oversee elections,” said Massachusetts Attorney General General Andrea Joy Campbell. “Mail-in voting is secure, our election laws are strong, and there is absolutely no evidence of widespread voter fraud. I will not back down from ensuring that every eligible voter in Massachusetts can cast their ballot and have their vote counted.”
findings.note: Bennington Banner quotes Campbell from the coalition press release on the 2026 suit over the executive order titled Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections (mail voting and citizenship verification). Page date is the article date, which may be a day or so after the filing.
